messages:
ana: quick heads-up — customer A on Dedicated hit soft-eviction yesterday and we spilled requests to hosted variants. they flagged data residency concerns, asking why spillover ever happened. can we recap current default behavior and whether tenants can opt-out?

mike: short answer: default is to allow spillover to compatible hosted model-variants when dedicated pool is exhausted unless tenant has explicit isolation flag. but the signal flow is messy — quota vs capacity vs routing policy.

li: i saw the trace — router matched policy: tier=standard -> fallback=hosted_compatible, model_variant=quantized-lite. no tenant header indicating opt-out.

ana: @li you mean ana? (typo)

ana: oops meant ana :facepalm: (ignore)

ana: @mike that's helpful. the ask from CS is: for Dedicated customers with PII/regulatory requirements we should have a "hard isolation" mode that prevents any external routing. also need an audit event when spillover is attempted.

sasha: agreed. two quick design choices: (1) make isolation an explicit tenant property enforced in router (deny on capacity overflow), or (2) keep current spillover but require tenant to opt-in to isolation which triggers circuit-breaker instead of spillover.

mike: tradeoffs: (1) could cause tight capacity interactions (customers will go down more often), (2) increases customer support but provides stronger guarantees. either way we need telemetry: per-tenant spillover_count, spillover_ratio, last_spill_ts.

li: also need to think about model-variant fallback: some hosted variants run on shared infra with different quantization. for sensitive tenants we must avoid variants that do not have encryption-in-flight or cert pinning. currently we only check model architecture compatibility.

ana: do we have an internal API field for the router to annotate requests? e.g. X-Redwood-Served-From: dedicated|hosted; should that be surfaced to customer logs?

mike: we already attach X-Serving-Mode but it's internal-only. exposing it to customer logs is an infra + security question. could leak topology. maybe surface a boolean in audit events instead.

li: proposal for a small config change (pseudo YAML):
```yaml
tenant_policies:
  tenant_id: cust-A
  isolation_mode: HARD # HARD | SOFT | DEFAULT
  allow_spillover_variants: ["redwood/quantized-lite"]
  audit_on_spill: true
```
this would let router honor tenant policy and also limit which variants are acceptable.

sasha: UX ask for Console: add a per-tenant toggle (isolation: HARD/SOFT), show recent spillover events in timeline, and a soft warning during rollout telling customers what will happen if they enable HARD. also make it part of Dedicated onboarding checklist.

ana: incremental engineering plan idea: 1) add per-tenant flag and block-in-router, 2) emit audit event "spillover_attempted" with fields: tenant_id, source_pool, attempted_variant, decision, reason, 3) expose metric spillover_ratio on tenant dashboard.

mike: implementation notes: router needs fast path: check tenant policy cache (inlined Redis) before fallback. if HARD -> fail with 429/spillover_disallowed. if SOFT -> continue fallback but tag event. also add unit test for eviction -> fallback.

li: important: ensure we don't change default behavior unexpectedly. need a rollout plan and feature-flag gate. add telemetry-first rollout: enable audit events for small percentage of tenants to validate.

infra-bot: created ticket INF-8426: "tenant isolation flags + spillover audit events" assigned to sasha, linked PR template.

sasha: i'll pick up the router changes. i'll propose API shape for tenant policy endpoint tomorrow and a Console mock later this week. tagging @mike @li for review.

ana: perfect. CS will prepare a FAQ and update onboarding docs. thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: one more open question: should router redact model_variant names in audit events for privacy? or we keep full variant id for debugging? thoughts?

li: keep full id internally, redact when exporting to customer-facing logs. add an export flag.

ana: ok locking that in for now. we'll iterate if legal asks more.

sasha: logging note -> include trace_id and route_decision in event. PR will include schema.

ana: end — will follow up on status in next eng-platform sync.
